title: Nordics enterprise launch playbook
body:
Purpose

This playbook is a working internal draft to align GTM, sales engineering, product, and marketing for Redwood’s Nordics enterprise launch (targeting Sweden/Denmark/Norway/Finland). Focus: Dedicated + Private offerings for regulated, latency-sensitive SaaS and finance verticals.

Target launch window
- Soft beta outreach: 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-30
- Broad regional announcement: 2026-05-12

Primary objectives (90 days post-launch)
- 6 committed POCs across fintech and healthcare orgs in Sweden/Denmark/Norway
- Achieve sub-50ms median token latency for enterprise dedicated configs in Stockholm region during 95th percentile traffic windows
- Create 8 customer-ready sales decks and 3 recorded demos localized for Nordic audiences

Key audiences and personas
- Platform/ML Engineer (primary): cares about latency SLAs, model version pinning, VPC/private control plane. Sales hooks: predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency, private deployment options.
- Head of Product / CTO (buyer): cares about time-to-market, compliance, vendor lock-in risk. Sales hooks: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private; migration path; cost controls.
- Security & Compliance Officer: cares about data residency, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations. Sales hooks: Private deployments, audit trails, SOC2/GDPR references.

Positioning statement (Nordics, enterprise)
"Redwood Inference: The production-first inference platform engineered for predictable latency, lower unit cost, and enterprise controls — now with Nordics capacity and private deployment options for regulated and latency-sensitive teams."

Top three GTM messages (short)
1) Predictable performance where it matters — dedicated pools in Stockholm with SLOs you can commit to.
2) Enterprise privacy and control — private control plane + KMS integrations meet Nordic compliance needs.
3) Move faster without reengineering — same API, tooling, and rollout controls across hosted → dedicated → private.

Differentiation vs primary competitors (notes for quick reference)
- AWS Bedrock / Vendor endpoints: Strength is deep cloud integration and account stickiness. Redwood win: lower predictable per-token cost for sustained inference; unified rollout tooling across private and hosted; clear performance SLOs for bursty token workloads.
- OpenAI (hosted): Strength is model quality and ecosystem. Redwood win: enterprise deployment flexibility (private/VPC + on-prem options), regional capacity footprint, and explicit cost/performance tuning (batching, quantization recommendations).
- Local EU/Scandi providers (smaller inference vendors): Strength: regional presence. Redwood win: production-grade runtime, proven autoscaling for dedicated pools, enterprise observability and rollout features.
- Self-hosted stacks (customers building in-house): Strength: control. Redwood win: lower engineering ops burden, faster time-to-production, fallback policies, and managed optimizations that preserve latency while reducing unit cost.

Key objections and suggested responses
- "We already have a vendor in AWS with deep integration." → Ask about current token economics and latency SLO gaps; demo predictable throughput and compare 95th/99th latency numbers. Offer a technical POC to measure real workload.
- "Data residency / compliance concerns." → Walk through Private deployment options, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and customer references (anonymized). Bring in security PM.
- "We can build this ourselves." → Outline expected infra/ops hours, maintenance surface, and recent benchmarks showing unit-cost delta and time-to-feature. Offer proof-of-value pilot.

Sales enablement assets to ship (owner / ETA)
- One-pager: Nordics Enterprise Value Props (Marcus) — 2026-03-20
- Technical one-pager: Deployment Options & Security (Priya) — 2026-03-24
- Demo scripts (recorded): Dedicated capacity deep dive (SE team) — 2026-03-28
- Competitive cheat sheet: Nordics vs AWS/OpenAI/local (Anika) — 2026-03-15 (v1)
- Pricing scenarios spreadsheet (sheet): dedicated commitment tiers mapped to throughput and expected unit cost (Finance) — 2026-03-22

Launch channels and suggested cadence
- Week 0 (internal): All-hands briefing + enablement Q&A (recording, FAQ)
- Week 1 (soft outreach): Targeted POC invites (existing ARR > $200k accounts in region)
- Week 3 (announce): Regional blog + email to product/engineering audience, partner co-marketing posts (local cloud partners)
- Ongoing: Monthly customer webinars (tech deep dives) and region-focused case studies

Draft internal announcement (for internal channels / Slack + email)
Subject: Nordics enterprise launch — enablement + playbook available\\nHi team,

We’re launching Redwood’s Nordics enterprise offering focused on Dedicated and Private deployments, with target capacity in Stockholm and immediate enablement materials for SEs and AEs. Primary focus: regulated and latency-sensitive customers (fintech, healthcare, GovTech).

What’s available now: playbook, demo recordings, pricing scenarios, and security one-pager. Link: [confluence link]. Please watch the enablement recording (30m) and add questions to #gtm-nordics.

If you have prioritized accounts in the region, flag them to the SE rota — we’ll run first POC offers starting 2026-04-06.

— Anika

Sample customer outreach email (for AEs)
Subject: Pilot Redwood dedicated inference in Stockholm for <COMPANY>
Hi <FirstName>,

Quick note — we’re running a limited pilot for enterprise teams in the Nordics to test dedicated inference capacity in Stockholm (predictable latency + private deployment options). If you have latency-sensitive features or compliance constraints, we can run a 4–6 week POC and share real workload metrics.

Interested? I can set up a short tech scoping call with our SEs.

Thanks,
<Name>

Demo runbook (short)
- 0:00 Intro + use-case framing (2m)
- 2:00 Architecture overview: hosted → dedicated → private (4m)
- 6:00 Live latency demo: 95th/99th percentile comparison (8m)
- 14:00 Security & compliance: audit logs, KMS (4m)
- 18:00 Rollout controls: canary/A-B/fallback (3m)
- 21:00 Q&A + next steps (9m)

Measurement and KPIs
- POC conversion rate (POC started → POC paid) target: 40%
- Median token latency (dedicated Stockholm) target: <50ms at p95
- Number of enablement assets produced: 8 baseline (decks, one-pagers, demos)
- Early revenue target (90 days): $300k ARR committed via dedicated contracts

Localization and partner notes (practical)
- Translate key one-pagers to Swedish and Danish (content team) — v1 by 2026-04-01
- Engage local cloud partners and SI firms for managed integration (Óscar) — start outreach 2026-03-10
- Consider local compliance certs list per country (legal + security)

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm regional pricing buckets with Finance (JIRA-4627) — Owner: Finance (due 2026-03-18)
- Technical SE checklist for private deployment in Stockholm region — Owner: SE lead (Priya) — due 2026-03-14
- Referenceable anonymized customer case studies for compliance/latency — ask Customer Success for candidates (Marcus)

Notes to self (working)
- Consider making a short A/B page that compares "predictable dedicated" vs "best-effort hosted" for quick AE use.
- Track latency SLO story in Redwood Console screenshots for the deck.

Appendix: quick competitive bullets for AEs (one-liners)
- AWS: strong integration; call out sustained cost and inability to guarantee cross-instance SLOs for bursty LLM workloads.
- OpenAI: best for experimentation; for enterprise compliance & private deployments, Redwood offers clear path to on-prem/VPC.
- Local small vendors: great for region-only needs but lack mature rollout tooling and observability.

Last updated: 2026-03-03 (Anika)

End of doc
